title: Default Report And Analysis Tags Refactor Delivery
summary: define the docs_subscope default and refactor Analysis Tags onto the standard registered customisation framework
content_html:
Default Report And Analysis Tags Refactor Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as SSR-1, the first delivery under Sub-Scope Report Defaults And Customisations.

This delivery defines the default docs_subscope report, implements one standard registered customisation boundary, and refactors Analysis/Tags to use default behaviour plus explicit customisations. It does not change the sub-scope lifecycle or decide Projects behaviour.

Working notes are the temporary product input for SSR-1.0. This delivery and the architecture become the authority once the specification is locked.

Development uses an isolated local-only candidate so the shipped Analysis/Tags report remains on the current canonical implementation until default and Tags parity are both ready for one cutover.

Complete Outcome

A minimally configured sub-scope renders the same list/detail engine with title search, normal empty/error states, compact Manage rows, title/recency sorting, New, selection, Prepare Package, validated-detail Delete and Copy Link, plus app-level Import context. It needs no Analysis/Tags config or module.

studio/default is the reference collection. Its feature-child report host and builder-generated empty/populated manifests exercise the candidate during development. At completion that host uses canonical docs_subscope; no candidate report identity remains.

Analysis/Tags selects one known customisation identity. Its current public and Manage behaviour is preserved, but its group projection and filtering are composed through its own module rather than wired into the shared report.

Fixed Boundaries

  • One shared docs_subscope engine remains the rendering and navigation owner.
  • A temporary local-only candidate may copy the shared report module and use a separate default Manage contribution; it is removed during accepted cutover and is never a compatibility layer or second shipped report.
  • The current canonical docs_subscope and Analysis/Tags contribution remain unchanged until the candidate and Tags customisation pass their respective gates.
  • The candidate reuses the normal sub-scope builder, manifests, and generic helpers. It does not fork data generation or exact-target semantics.
  • Config selects only a known customisation identity; the registry owns module resolution.
  • Public routes import no Manage customisation code or capability data.
  • Title search is default. Additional filters are customisations.
  • New, status/viewability row treatment, title/recency sorting, selection, Prepare Package, validated-detail Delete and Copy Link are default Manage behaviour.
  • Default order is title ascending. The Manage toggle switches to last_updated descending with missing values last and title/doc_id tie-breakers.
  • Copy Link reuses the existing Markdown viewer-link convention with the exact validated sub-scope detail URL.
  • The standard Manage manifest adds last_updated; collection-specific fields such as Analysis/Tags group come only from the selected customisation.
  • Import remains app-level and consumes only a mounted exact collection.
  • No Analysis/Tags identifier, label, group value, or manifest filename may be a dispatcher condition.
  • No compatibility adapter remains after the Analysis/Tags path reaches parity unless separately justified with removal criteria.

Delivery Checkpoints

[ ] SSR-1.0 — Freeze Default And Module Contract

  • [ ] Trace current shared report, filter toolbar, Manage contribution, action definitions, capability projection, and Analysis/Tags config.
  • [ ] Freeze the customisation config field, safe registry shape, public/Manage loading boundary, and unknown-identity failure.
  • [x] Freeze the default public and Manage row fields, including last_updated for recency sorting.
  • [x] Freeze title-ascending initial order, recency-descending alternate order, missing-value placement, and stable tie-breakers.
  • [x] Make status/viewability, New, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, Copy Link, and Import-context publication default; classify group projection and filtering as the Analysis/Tags customisation.
  • [ ] Freeze row, filter, list-toolbar, selection, detail-toolbar, and lifecycle contribution payloads.
  • [ ] Freeze the builder-side customisation projection paired with each known browser module identity.

Checkpoint: one reviewed contract names the default, every retained Tags feature, its target, owner, access boundary, and refresh effect. Stop before runtime edits.

[ ] SSR-1.1 — Build The Isolated Default Candidate

  • [ ] Register one explicitly temporary local-only candidate loader over a copy of the current shared report module; add no public loader entry.
  • [ ] Configure studio/default with no customisation identity and create one feature-child host pointing at the candidate during development.
  • [ ] Build its normal empty manifest.json and manage-manifest.json, then add only the representative child fixtures needed to prove accepted row fields and states.
  • [ ] Give the candidate a separate default Manage composition so changes do not affect the existing Analysis/Tags toolbar.
  • [ ] Make the minimally configured candidate render without Analysis/Tags fields.
  • [ ] Keep title search in the shared default and place non-default filters behind the customisation boundary.
  • [ ] Add the controlled identity resolver and public-safe/Manage module split.
  • [ ] Render capability-gated exact-collection New for empty and populated manageable collections.
  • [ ] Add the Manage sort toggle and standard last_updated projection without changing public manifest shape.
  • [ ] Add validated-detail Copy Link using the existing Markdown-link convention and exact report-host/subdoc URL.
  • [ ] Cover missing config, unknown identity, empty collection, unavailable capability, invalid target, remount, and public isolation.

Checkpoint: the candidate works independently on studio/default, the canonical Analysis/Tags path is unchanged, and the contract can add one row feature, filter, list action, selection action, and detail action. Stop before moving Analysis/Tags.

[ ] SSR-1.2 — Refactor Analysis/Tags And Cut Over

  • [ ] Register the Analysis/Tags customisation through sub-scope config.
  • [ ] Move the group Manage-manifest projection, configured group order, and group controls/filtering out of the default into the Analysis/Tags customisation.
  • [ ] Consume the remaining status/viewability, sorting, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, Copy Link, and Import-context features unchanged from the default.
  • [ ] Preserve configured Tags/Concepts titles, group order, manifest isolation, Back/Forward, selection, exact targets, and refresh behaviour.
  • [ ] After default acceptance and Tags parity, make the accepted candidate the canonical docs_subscope implementation and switch the Studio host to it.
  • [ ] Remove the candidate report registry row, loader entry, temporary Manage dispatch, and superseded direct wiring in the same cutover.

Checkpoint: Analysis/Tags is a consumer of the default, owns its additional composition, and has no separate report implementation, candidate alias, or hidden dispatcher.

[ ] SSR-1.3 — Verification And Authority Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused generator/config, runtime-module, contribution, action-target, public-import-boundary, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Manually review default empty/list/detail and current Analysis/Tags public and Manage states at representative widths.
  • [ ] Inspect the final diff independently and separate fixture coverage from live-route observation.
  • [ ] Update the durable Sub-Scope Index architecture, manifest, and toolbar owners only where shipped contracts changed.
  • [ ] Stop for review before starting SSR-2.

Out Of Scope

  • creating report hosts or manifests from lifecycle mutation;
  • changing child inclusion in parent discovery;
  • Projects-specific config or behaviour;
  • Tag Registry mutation or field synchronisation;
  • a customisation framework for unrelated reports; and
  • additional toolbar actions without an accepted exact target and capability contract.

Completion Gates

  • The default works with no collection customisation.
  • studio/default uses canonical docs_subscope, and no temporary candidate registry, loader, dispatch, or module identity remains.
  • Analysis/Tags uses a configured registered module and preserves accepted behaviour.
  • The default and dispatcher contain no Analysis/Tags special case.
  • Public projections and imports remain isolated from Manage code and data.
  • Every action consumes only its explicit collection, checked IDs, or validated document target.
  • Standard last_updated has a visible report use and deterministic missing-value handling.
  • Future collections can add registered data projections and browser contributions without adding their IDs, fields, or workflows to the default engine.
  • Durable documentation matches the shipped extension rule.
